summary: Okta SSO fails for feature-flag console after IdP header size enforcement
description:
Issue summary: Several internal engineers report they cannot log in to the feature-flagging console. Login attempts redirect back to Okta and then return a 400 from the auth proxy. Impact: Blocks ~12 engineers from toggling flags and viewing rollout state in prod-us-east. No external customers affected, but a high operational impact for releases planned today.

Observed behaviour: Users authenticate successfully at Okta; after Okta redirect the auth-proxy returns 400 and the console shows 'Login failed'. This began after IdP announced header size enforcement (removing oversized headers) earlier today.

Business impact: P1 – operational runway for a production release is degraded.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open feature-flag console (https://flags.redwood.example) in chrome (incognito recommended).
3) Complete Okta MFA flow and allow redirect back to console.
4) Observe auth-proxy returns 400 and console shows generic login failure.
observed_error_messages: browser console: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400 (Bad Request)
logs: 2026-03-12T09:12:03Z auth-proxy us-east-1 pod-23: incoming request /auth/callback size 67512 bytes -> rejected: header_too_large
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z auth-proxy us-east-1 pod-23: x-forwarded-for: 10.1.2.3, cookie length: 67000
2026-03-12T09:12:05Z okta-webhook: user john.doe@example.com completed authentication, returned redirect to https://flags.redwood.example/auth/callback?state=...&code=...
2026-03-12T09:12:05Z feature-flag-console us-east-1 pod-4: received 400 from auth-proxy when handling callback
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: IdP header truncation/enforcement removed or modified a long cookie/header leading to mismatch in auth-proxy parsing logic.
Reproduced in prod-us-east with synthetic user; request headers show a single cookie with long JSON blob used by legacy session glue (pre-prod consolidation).

Auth-proxy recently had nginx upgrade (2026-03-10) which enabled stricter header-size defaults; review of nginx.conf shows client_header_buffer_size and large_client_header_buffers set to default values.

Okta confirmed they rolled out a header-size enforcement change at ~2026-03-12T08:50Z for our tenant (reference OKTA-OPS ticket), which removed duplicate long Set-Cookie header introduced by a legacy tracking middleware.
Workaround discovered: clearing browser cookies for *.redwood.example allows successful login; shorter cookie payloads work.
comments: Maya Thompson (reporter) 2026-03-12: Reported after trying to onboard a release toggling. Noticed several teammates with same symptoms.
Diego Ramirez (assignee) 2026-03-12: Acknowledged, running pod-level captures and nginx error logs. Suspect header size enforcement; starting mitigation plan.
SRE Team 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation - increase large_client_header_buffers on auth-proxy to accept current cookie sizes, and add server-side normalization to strip legacy tracking cookie.
Security 2026-03-13: Flag - confirm removing/trimming cookies does not leak PII. Confirmed legacy tracking cookie contains no PII but must be redacted before downstream services see it.
Product Eng 2026-03-14: Requested ETA on permanent fix so we can resume scheduled flag flips for release tomorrow.
resolution: Mitigation applied: increased nginx large_client_header_buffers in auth-proxy deployment in prod-us-east and deployed a header-normalizer sidecar that strips legacy __rf_track cookie. Workaround for users: clear cookies for .redwood.example. Permanent follow-ups: remove legacy tracking middleware from upstream services (ENG-FF-921), add cookie-length monitoring alert, and coordinate with Okta to revert tenant header enforcement once cleanup is complete. Status: mitigation in place; monitoring for 24h.
